pageTitle: Wah Pedals: Resonant Bandpass Filters, Inductors & Vocal Expression
subtitle: The human voice of the electric guitar — Fasel inductors, potentiometers, swept resonant peaks & iconic funk/rock expressions

introduction.title: Wah Pedals: Resonant Bandpass Filters, Inductors & Vocal Expression
introduction.text:
The wah-wah pedal is the most dynamically expressive and physical effect in guitar history. Unlike stompboxes that operate with a simple on/off click, a wah pedal is an active foot-controlled acoustic instrument. Rocking the treadle back and forth physically sweeps a narrow, highly resonant bandpass filter across the audio frequency spectrum—boosting a focused peak by +15dB to +18dB while rolling off frequencies above and below it. Because this sweep moves through the exact acoustic formant frequencies of the human vocal tract (shifting from deep 'oo' at 350Hz to open 'ah' at 900Hz and piercing 'ee' at 2.5kHz), it imparts an uncanny human speech-like expression to electric guitar notes.

Invented accidentally in November 1966 by Thomas Organ engineer Brad Plunkett while developing a cheap transistorized mid-boost circuit for the Vox Super Beatle amplifier, the pedal was immediately endorsed by trumpeter Clyde McCoy (whose muted 'wah-wah' horn style the pedal evoked). When Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton (with Cream), and funk legends like Charles Pitts ('Theme from Shaft') harnessed its percussive rhythmic potential, the wah pedal became an indelible cultural icon. From percussive 16th-note funk rhythm chops to screaming stadium rock lead solos and stationary 'cocked wah' studio filters, mastering the wah pedal connects your foot directly to your musical soul.
introduction.quote: A wah pedal does not merely process your sound; it sings. By sweeping a resonant filter peak through human vocal formant frequencies in real time, it transforms cold guitar strings into a crying, laughing, screaming human voice.

cards.title: The Resonant LCR Bandpass Filter
cards.description: At the heart of every classic wah pedal is a tuned Inductor-Capacitor-Resistor (LCR) bandpass filter circuit driven by a single bipolar transistor. As you rock the mechanical treadle, a rack-and-pinion gear rotates a specialized 100kΩ potentiometer. This shifts the resonant center frequency of the filter continuously from approximately 350Hz (heel-down) up to 2.5kHz (toe-down), while applying a massive +15dB to +18dB resonant boost with a sharp 'Q' factor (filter steepness).

fields.label: Heel-Down Position
fields.value: Resonant peak at ~350Hz–450Hz; deep, muffled, dark 'oo' vowel sound

fields.label: Mid-Treadle Position
fields.value: Resonant peak at ~750Hz–1kHz; punchy, open, vocal 'ah' vowel sound

fields.label: Toe-Down Position
fields.value: Resonant peak at ~2.2kHz–2.5kHz; bright, piercing, aggressive 'ee' vowel sound

fields.label: The Resonant Q Peak
fields.value: Sharp +15dB to +18dB boost pushes downstream tube preamps into sweet harmonic overdrive

items: Matches the natural formant vowel frequencies of the human mouth when speaking or singing
Rocking the foot in rhythm with the picking hand produces articulate 'wacka-wacka' funk grooves
Sweeping the pedal slowly through a sustained bend creates dramatic vocal cries on blues and rock solos

cards.title: The Fasel Inductor & Treadle Potentiometers
cards.description: The inductor is the vital electromagnetic component that dictates the personality, harmonic warmth, and sweep curve of a wah pedal. Original 1960s Italian Vox wahs utilized toroidal Fasel inductors made in Italy. As guitar voltage passes through the inductor's magnetic core, subtle magnetic saturation adds rich analog harmonics and smooths off harsh treble peaks.

fields.label: Red Fasel Inductor
fields.value: Toroidal design; aggressive, modern harmonic bite with clean, cutting high-end punch

fields.label: Yellow Fasel Inductor
fields.value: Cup-core design; warm, vintage vocal sweep with smooth, rounded high-frequency roll-off

fields.label: Halo Inductor
fields.value: Vintage 1960s spec; woody, hollow midrange with wide, expressive vocal dynamics

fields.label: 100k Hot Potz Potentiometer
fields.value: Specially tapered audio pot sealed against dust and debris, engineered for millions of sweeps

items: Modern optical wahs (like Morley) replace potentiometers with LEDs and shutter flaps, eliminating scratchy pot noise
Inductor saturation prevents high-gain distortion from turning into shrill, ice-pick frequencies at the toe-down position
Changing the pinion gear alignment on the pot shaft allows customizing the sweep range to your personal preference

sections.title: Legendary Benchmark Wah Pedals
sections.subtitle: The industry-standard stompboxes dominating funk, rock, and metal history

cards.title: Dunlop Cry Baby GCB95
cards.description: The undisputed king of wah pedals. Found on more professional stages and hit records than any other effect pedal in history, the GCB95 features a heavy die-cast zinc housing, custom-voiced Red Fasel inductor, and a 100k Hot Potz potentiometer that delivers cutting, aggressive rock and funk sweep.

fields.label: Inductor
fields.value: Authentic Italian-made Red Fasel inductor for punchy, vocal harmonic response

fields.label: Switching
fields.value: Heavy-duty mechanical toe-switch with durable rubber bumpers

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: Jimi Hendrix, Slash (Guns N' Roses), Kirk Hammett (Metallica), Buddy Guy

items: The driving voice behind Slash's iconic solo on 'Sweet Child O' Mine' and Kirk Hammett's blistering thrash leads
Indestructible die-cast housing built to withstand decades of violent, heavy-footed stage stomping
Cuts through loud drum kits and high-gain half-stacks with immediate frequency clarity

cards.title: Dunlop Cry Baby Mini
cards.description: All the legendary Cry Baby tone in a housing half the size of standard pedals. Designed to save precious pedalboard real estate, the CBM95 features an authentic Red Fasel inductor, true hardwire bypass, and an internal 3-position voicing switch.

fields.label: Form Factor
fields.value: Half the footprint of a standard GCB95; weighs only 0.45 kg (0.99 lbs)

fields.label: Internal Voicing Switch
fields.value: Low (dark, bass-heavy sweep), Vintage (warm, vocal mid sweep), and GCB95 (aggressive modern bite)

fields.label: Bypass Mode
fields.value: True hardwire bypass eliminates vintage 'tone suck' when the pedal is disengaged

items: Saves over 50% pedalboard width while retaining a fully usable, comfortable foot sweep
Vintage voicing switch setting tames overly bright single-coil bridge pickups
Rigid aluminum construction engineered for worldwide fly-dates and touring rigs

cards.title: Vox V847
cards.description: The direct descendant of the original 1967 British wah that started it all. Featuring authentic vintage-spec circuitry, chrome-plated treadle, warm vocal frequency response, and an included vinyl carry bag, the V847 delivers the warm, expressive sweep of late-1960s psychedelic rock.

fields.label: Voicing Character
fields.value: Warmer, wider, more vocal midrange sweep than the aggressive Cry Baby

fields.label: Aesthetics
fields.value: Chrome-plated treadle with classic embossed VOX rubber pad and black crinkle chassis

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: Eric Clapton (Cream - 'White Room'), Jimi Hendrix, Frank Zappa

items: The quintessential wah sound heard on Cream's 'White Room' and 'Tales of Brave Ulysses'
Warmer high-end roll-off makes it the premier pairing for vintage fuzz pedals and bright Marshall Plexi amps
Buffered input stage preserves clean signal strength across long pedalboard cable runs

cards.title: Ibanez WH10
cards.description: The unique op-amp driven wah pedal that defined the sound of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Unlike inductor-based wahs, the WH10 utilizes multiple feedback operational amplifier filters with an adjustable Depth knob and a dedicated Guitar/Bass frequency range switch.

fields.label: Filter Circuit
fields.value: Multiple feedback active op-amp filter (no inductor); wide, smooth frequency sweep

fields.label: Depth Knob
fields.value: Controls the intensity and boost level of the resonant frequency sweep (+6dB to +20dB boost)

fields.label: Guitar / Bass Switch
fields.value: Shifts frequency sweep down an octave for electric bass or drop-tuned guitars

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: John Frusciante (Blood Sugar Sex Magik, Californication, Stadium Arcadium)

items: The driving force behind John Frusciante's screaming funk-rock solos on 'Dani California' and 'Can't Stop'
The onboard boost slams front-end tube amplifiers into instant soaring harmonic feedback when engaged
Modern V3 reissue features rugged die-cast aluminum housing and switchable true/buffered bypass

sections.title: The 'Cocked Wah' Studio Secret & Expressive Techniques
sections.subtitle: How legendary guitarists use wah pedals without moving their feet

cards.title: The Stationary 'Cocked Wah' Filter Trick
cards.description: One of the most famous studio production tricks in rock history is the 'Cocked Wah' (leaving the wah pedal turned ON, but parking the treadle in a fixed, stationary position about halfway forward). This transforms the pedal into a razor-sharp, narrow parametric equalizer, boosting a laser-focused frequency band around 1kHz–1.5kHz while filtering out flubby lows and harsh highs.

fields.label: Treadle Position
fields.value: Parked stationary between 40% and 60% forward sweep

fields.label: Acoustic Effect
fields.value: Creates a focused, honky, nasally midrange peak that cuts through dense walls of drums and bass

fields.label: Famous Masterpieces
fields.value: Mark Knopfler on Dire Straits' 'Money for Nothing', Mick Ronson on Bowie's 'Ziggy Stardust', Michael Schenker

items: Eliminates mud in multi-tracked rock rhythm guitars, making single-note riffs punch out with authority
Creates the unmistakable metallic, vocal bite heard on the intro riff to Dire Straits' 'Money for Nothing'
Modern pedal manufacturers make dedicated fixed 'cocked wah' stompboxes (e.g. Dunlop Q-Zone, Electro-Harmonix Cock Fight)

cards.title: Percussive 16th-Note Funk Rhythms
cards.description: In funk, soul, and R&B music, the wah pedal is played as a percussive rhythm instrument rather than a melodic filter. By muting the guitar strings lightly across the fretboard with the left hand (fret-hand muting) and picking continuous 16th-note patterns with the right hand, the wah pedal's foot sweep creates the iconic 'wacka-wacka' sound.

fields.label: Fret Hand
fields.value: Lightly touch strings across the frets without depressing them to produce muted percussive clicks

fields.label: Pick Hand
fields.value: Continuous, steady alternate picking (down-up-down-up) in crisp 16th-note meter

fields.label: Foot Treadle
fields.value: Rock heel-to-toe on downbeats and toe-to-heel on upbeats in sync with the drummer's hi-hat

items: The defining soundtrack of 1970s blaxploitation cinema (Charles Pitts on Isaac Hayes' 'Theme from Shaft')
Transforms simple percussive scratching into an expressive, rhythmic groove machine
Essential technique for funk, disco, modern neo-soul, and reggae skank rhythm guitar

sections.title: Pedalboard Routing & The Fuzz-Wah Oscillation Problem
sections.subtitle: How to wire wah pedals correctly and eliminate vintage buffer squeal

cards.title: Wah BEFORE Distortion vs. AFTER Distortion
cards.description: The physical placement of a wah pedal relative to your overdrive, distortion, and fuzz pedals completely changes its acoustic behavior.

fields.label: Wah BEFORE Distortion (Standard)
fields.value: Guitar → WAH → Distortion → Amp: Vocal, organic, smooth filter sweep; the standard rock/funk sound

fields.label: Wah AFTER Distortion (Aggressive)
fields.value: Guitar → Distortion → WAH → Amp: Extreme, screaming, synth-like resonant sweep with dramatic frequency spikes

fields.label: High-Gain Solos
fields.value: Wah into distortion softens the resonant peak, preventing piercing high-frequency ear fatigue

items: 95% of guitarists place wah first: sweeping a clean signal before distortion produces natural, expressive vocal sweeps
Placing wah after distortion filters the distorted harmonics, producing extreme, dramatic sweep effects (used by Tom Morello and Cliff Burton)

cards.title: The Fuzz-Wah Buffer Oscillation Problem
cards.description: Placing a vintage wah pedal (like an unbuffered Cry Baby) in front of a vintage two-transistor fuzz pedal (like a Fuzz Face) often produces an ear-piercing high-frequency oscillation squeal, loss of sweep range, or thin nasal tone when both pedals are stomped on together. This occurs because the wah's output impedance clashes with the fuzz's low-impedance input.

fields.label: The Cause
fields.value: Impedance mismatch between the wah's inductor output and the fuzz's Q1 input transistor induces parasitic feedback

fields.label: The Solution
fields.value: Use a wah pedal equipped with an output buffer circuit (or insert an active buffer between wah and fuzz)

fields.label: Jimi Hendrix Secret
fields.value: Roger Mayer modified Hendrix's wah pedals with discrete output buffer stages to cure this exact squeal on stage

items: Modern wahs (like the Dunlop Cry Baby Classic and Clyde McCoy reissues) include built-in output buffers to allow flawless fuzz stacking
Eliminates feedback squeal and restores full, rich low-to-high frequency sweep when soloing through heavy fuzz
Allows running Wah → Fuzz Face → Tube Amp without sonic degradation or loss of sweep dynamics
